The practical orthography (ɔ ɛ ɨ ŋ, ch ny kp gb) carries no tone or accent diacritics in either chapter read, so it yields neither a statement nor tone-marked data. It does show that LIST ran two Luke projects (Nkome 2022, Olulumo-Ikom 2024), so two project-internal orthography statements presumably exist offline.

sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: Scripture text only, no orthography statement. The practical orthography uses ɛ, ɔ, ɨ, ŋ and digraphs (ny, kp, gb) and carries NO tone or accent diacritics (e.g. 'Kegbu kanci, Ɔkɨm Ɛmaŋ Ɔgɔstus ɔjɛ nsɨm ya oni naŋɔnɛ..'), so it yields neither a statement nor marked prosodic data. An orthography guide presumably exists within the LIST/Seed Company project but is not online.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A comparative study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu languages. Vol. II. Oxford: Clarendon Press. [Remarks on no. 238 Olulɔmɔ and 238a Ikom in the chapters on prefixes/concords and pronouns, pp. 234-235 and passim in the root analyses.]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on prosody. Content is comparative morphology: loss of initial M- in class 1 prefix, Ke-/Bi- (7/8), Ja-, En-, Ma-, Je-, Da-/Ra- plural prefixes, diminutive Won- 'child', 2pl pronoun Wun, plus scattered lexical root comparisons citing 238. The phonology chapters do not single out 238/238a.
